BestBirdwatching

Rainforest, wetland, seabird cliff and migration bottleneck — the places that hold either the highest species counts on earth or the birds you cannot see anywhere else. Almost every one of them works on a calendar: a migration trap is empty outside its three weeks, a crane roost fills only in winter, and a cloud-forest endemic is easiest in its own short breeding season.

Iberá Wetlands
Corrientes
Second-Largest Wetland in South America
A vast freshwater marsh system in north-eastern Argentina holding around 350 bird species, including the strange-tailed tyrant and the sickle-winged nightjar. Boat transects from Colonia Carlos Pellegrini put birders inside the reedbeds.
Wikipedia Map
Bruny Island
Tasmania
All 12 Tasmanian Endemics
An island off Hobart where every one of Tasmania's twelve endemic bird species can be seen, including the forty-spotted pardalote and the swift parrot. It is small enough to work the full list in two days.
Wikipedia Map
Kakadu National Park
Northern Territory
UNESCO World Heritage SiteAround 280 Species
A monsoon floodplain and sandstone escarpment park where the dry-season concentration on Yellow Water lagoon brings magpie geese, jabiru and comb-crested jacanas into one boat trip. Roughly a third of Australia's bird species have been recorded inside the park.
Wikipedia Map
Lamington National Park
Queensland
Gondwana RainforestsAlbert's Lyrebird
Subtropical rainforest on the Queensland–New South Wales border where regent and satin bowerbirds feed at arm's length around O'Reilly's and Albert's lyrebird displays in winter. The park is part of the Gondwana Rainforests World Heritage area.
Wikipedia Map
Okavango Delta
North-West District
UNESCO World Heritage SitePel's Fishing Owl
An inland delta where the Okavango River empties into the Kalahari, holding over 450 recorded species across permanent swamp, seasonal floodplain and dry island. Mokoro channels are the reliable way to find Pel's fishing owl and slaty egret.
Wikipedia Map
Intervales State Park
São Paulo
Atlantic Forest Endemics
A large tract of intact Atlantic Forest on the Serra de Paranapiacaba holding many of the biome's endemics, including the solitary tinamou and several antbird species. Trails run from the visitor centre and are open to guided night walks.
Wikipedia Map
Pantanal
Mato Grosso
UNESCO World Heritage SiteHyacinth Macaw
The world's largest tropical wetland, where the dry season strands fish in shrinking pools and concentrates jabiru, wood stork and heron in the thousands. The Transpantaneira road gives roadside access to hyacinth macaw and greater rhea.
Wikipedia Map
Point Pelee National Park
Ontario
May Warbler MigrationSouthernmost Point in Mainland Canada
A sand spit into Lake Erie that acts as the first landfall for songbirds crossing the lake in spring, delivering dense warbler falls in the first three weeks of May. It is the mainland's southernmost point and one of North America's best-known migration traps.
Wikipedia Map
Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta
Magdalena
Around 20 Endemic SpeciesSea to Snowline in 42 km
An isolated coastal massif rising from the Caribbean to 5,700 metres with the highest count of endemic bird species of any mountain range on earth. The San Lorenzo ridge above Minca is the standard access for the Santa Marta parakeet and screech owl.
Wikipedia Map
La Selva Biological Station
Sarapiquí, Heredia
Over 470 Species Recorded
A lowland rainforest research station on the Caribbean slope with more than 470 recorded species and a trail network built for early-morning work. Great green macaw and snowy cotinga are both regular.
Wikipedia Map
Monteverde Cloud Forest
Puntarenas
Resplendent QuetzalThree-Wattled Bellbird
A cloud forest reserve on the continental divide where resplendent quetzals nest between February and July and the three-wattled bellbird calls from the canopy. The reserve limits daily entry, so the trails stay quiet.
Wikipedia Map
Galápagos Islands
Galápagos Province
UNESCO World Heritage SiteDarwin's Finches
An archipelago where the birds have no fear of people, giving close views of waved albatross, flightless cormorant, and the finch radiation that shaped evolutionary theory. Each island holds different endemics, so the itinerary decides the list.
Wikipedia Galápagos Guide Map
Mindo and the Chocó Slope
Pichincha
Around 500 SpeciesAndean Cock-of-the-Rock Lek
A band of cloud forest on the western Andean slope an hour and a half from Quito, with hummingbird feeders, an Andean cock-of-the-rock lek and the Chocó endemics of the Milpe and Mashpi ridges. It is one of the highest bird densities reachable on a day trip from a capital city.
Wikipedia Map
Napo Lowlands
Orellana
Canopy TowersParrot Clay Licks
Amazonian lowland forest downstream of Coca where canopy towers and oxbow lakes put birders level with the treetops. The riverbank clay licks draw hundreds of parrots and macaws in the early morning.
Wikipedia Map
Bale Mountains National Park
Oromia
Sanetti PlateauEthiopian Endemics
An Afroalpine plateau and the Harenna cloud forest below it, holding the blue-winged goose, spot-breasted lapwing and Abyssinian catbird found nowhere else. The Sanetti road crosses above 4,000 metres and can be birded from the car.
Wikipedia Map
Hortobágy National Park
Hajdú-Bihar
UNESCO World Heritage SiteAutumn Crane Roost
Europe's largest continuous natural grassland, with fish ponds, alkaline pans and a saker falcon population. In October and November tens of thousands of common cranes roost here on their way south.
Wikipedia Map
Látrabjarg
Westfjords
14 km of Seabird CliffWesternmost Point in Europe
A 14-kilometre wall of cliff in the Westfjords holding one of the largest seabird colonies in the North Atlantic, with puffins nesting close enough to the clifftop path to photograph without a lens. Razorbills, guillemots and fulmars fill the ledges below.
Wikipedia Map
Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary
Arunachal Pradesh
Bugun Liocichla3,250 m to 500 m in One Road
An Eastern Himalayan sanctuary whose single track drops from 3,250 metres to the plains, passing through every forest belt in between. It is the only known site for the Bugun liocichla, described as new to science in 2006.
Wikipedia Map
Keoladeo National Park
Bharatpur, Rajasthan
UNESCO World Heritage SiteOver 360 Species
A man-made wetland built as a duck shoot for the Maharajas of Bharatpur and now a winter refuge for painted stork, Sarus crane and large numbers of migratory waterfowl. Cycle rickshaws work the internal bunds and are the standard way to bird it.
Wikipedia Map
Halmahera
North Maluku
Wallacea EndemicsStandardwing Bird-of-Paradise
An island east of Wallace's Line whose forests hold the Wallace's standardwing bird-of-paradise, which displays at dawn from a handful of known leks near Foli. Ivory-breasted pitta and paradise-crow are the other regional draws.
Wikipedia Map
Tangkoko Batuangus
North Sulawesi
Sulawesi EndemicsMaleo and Hornbills
A coastal reserve on the north-east tip of Sulawesi holding red-knobbed hornbill, Sulawesi dwarf kingfisher and the ground-nesting maleo. The same trails are the best-known site for spectral tarsier.
Wikipedia Map
Eilat
Southern District
Spring Raptor MigrationBottleneck Site
A desert town at the head of the Red Sea where the funnel between the Sinai and the Arabian deserts concentrates raptors and passerines in March and April. Counts of steppe buzzard and honey buzzard here run into the hundreds of thousands.
Wikipedia Map
Hula Valley
Northern District
500 Million Migrants a YearCrane Feeding Station
A drained and partly restored lake on the Syrian–African rift flyway, where an estimated half a billion birds pass twice a year. Winter holds tens of thousands of common cranes, fed on maize to keep them off the surrounding farmland.
Wikipedia Map
Izumi Plain
Kagoshima, Kyushu
Over 10,000 Wintering Cranes
Rice fields in southern Kyushu that hold the largest wintering concentration of hooded and white-naped cranes in the world, regularly over ten thousand birds. An observation centre overlooks the roost from October to March.
Wikipedia Map
Kushiro Shitsugen
Hokkaido
Red-Crowned CraneJapan's Largest Marsh
A marsh in eastern Hokkaido that holds the resident Japanese population of red-crowned crane, which winters at feeding stations at Tsurui and Akan. The birds display in the snow in February, which is the reason most people come.
Wikipedia Map
Kakamega Forest
Kakamega County
Only Guinea-Congo Rainforest in Kenya
The eastern remnant of the Guinea–Congolian rainforest belt, holding around forty bird species found nowhere else in Kenya, among them the great blue turaco and the blue-headed bee-eater. It is a forest island surrounded by farmland.
Wikipedia Map
Lake Nakuru National Park
Nakuru County
Rift Valley Soda LakeOver 450 Species
A shallow soda lake in the Rift Valley whose algae blooms draw lesser flamingo in numbers that vary with the water level. Great white pelican, African fish eagle and a fenced rhino population share the shoreline.
Wikipedia Map
Andasibe-Mantadia
Alaotra-Mangoro
Ground-RollersFive Endemic Bird Families
Eastern rainforest three hours from Antananarivo holding pitta-like and scaly ground-rollers, helmet vanga and the asities that make up Madagascar's endemic families. The indri call that carries over the forest is the other reason to be there at dawn.
Wikipedia Map
Danum Valley
Sabah, Borneo
Primary Dipterocarp ForestBornean Bristlehead
An unlogged lowland forest reserve in eastern Sabah with a canopy walkway and a bird list holding all eight Bornean hornbill species. The Bornean bristlehead, the island's only endemic bird family, is regular here.
Wikipedia Map
Celestún Biosphere Reserve
Yucatán
American FlamingoMangrove Estuary
A mangrove estuary on the Gulf coast of Yucatán where American flamingo feed in the shallows in numbers through the winter. Boat trips from the village run the ría past roosting frigatebirds and pelicans.
Wikipedia Map
El Triunfo Biosphere Reserve
Chiapas
Horned GuanCloud Forest Trek
Cloud forest on the Sierra Madre de Chiapas reached only on foot or by mule over two days, holding the horned guan, azure-rumped tanager and resplendent quetzal. Access is by permit and the season runs from February to May.
Wikipedia Map
Chitwan National Park
Bagmati
UNESCO World Heritage SiteOver 500 Species
Lowland Terai grassland and sal forest along the Rapti and Narayani rivers, with a list above 500 species including the Bengal florican and giant hornbill. Elephant grass, riverine forest and river channel each hold a different set.
Wikipedia Map
Texel
North Holland
Wadden SeaSpoonbill Colonies
A Wadden Sea island whose dunes, polders and salt marsh hold breeding spoonbill, avocet and Eurasian curlew, with wader roosts on the tidal flats at high water. The whole Wadden system is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Wikipedia Map
Tiritiri Matangi
Hauraki Gulf, Auckland
Predator-Free IslandTakahē and Kōkako
An open sanctuary island in the Hauraki Gulf cleared of mammalian predators and replanted by volunteers, now holding takahē, kōkako, stitchbird and saddleback. A ferry from Auckland makes it a day trip.
Wikipedia Map
Ulva Island
Stewart Island, Southland
Predator-FreeRifleman and Saddleback
A small predator-free island in Paterson Inlet off Stewart Island where rifleman, South Island saddleback and yellowhead feed low along the tracks. Stewart Island itself is the most reliable place to see a wild kiwi.
Wikipedia Map
Varanger Peninsula
Finnmark
Arctic SeaducksSteller's Eider
An Arctic peninsula on the Barents Sea where king eider, Steller's eider and long-tailed duck winter in the ice-free fjords. The Hornøya cliff off Vardø holds Brünnich's guillemot and puffin from March.
Wikipedia Map
Pipeline Road
Soberanía National Park, Colón
Christmas Bird Count Records
A wartime service road through lowland forest beside the Panama Canal, with a bird list of over 400 species along its length. Counts along this single road have repeatedly set world records for a 24-hour species total.
Wikipedia Map
Varirata National Park
Central Province
Raggiana Bird-of-Paradise Lek
A hill-forest park 45 minutes from Port Moresby with a known display tree for the Raggiana bird-of-paradise, the national bird. Growling riflebird and brown-headed paradise-kingfisher are both on the same trails.
Raggiana Bird-of-Paradise Map
Manú National Park
Madre de Dios
UNESCO World Heritage SiteOver 1,000 Species
A park running from Andean cloud forest down to Amazonian lowland with a bird list above a thousand species, the highest of any protected area in the world. The road down from Paucartambo crosses every elevation band on the way in.
Wikipedia Cusco Guide Map
Tambopata National Reserve
Madre de Dios
Chuncho Clay LickAmazon Lowlands
Lowland Amazon reserve upstream of Puerto Maldonado holding the Chuncho and Colorado clay licks, where hundreds of macaws and parrots gather at first light. Oxbow lakes nearby hold hoatzin and agami heron.
Wikipedia Map
Biebrza Marshes
Podlaskie
Aquatic WarblerLargest Marsh in Central Europe
An undrained river valley in north-east Poland holding the largest population of the globally threatened aquatic warbler, along with great snipe lekking and breeding spotted crake. Spring flooding is the season to go.
Wikipedia Map
Kruger National Park
Mpumalanga and Limpopo
Over 500 SpeciesBig Six Birds
A savanna park the size of a small country with a list above 500 species, including the six large birds — ground hornbill, kori bustard, martial eagle, lappet-faced vulture, Pel's fishing owl and saddle-billed stork — that visitors work through. Self-drive access means the birding needs no guide.
Wikipedia Map
West Coast National Park
Western Cape
Langebaan LagoonSummer Wader Roost
A lagoon and strandveld park 90 minutes north of Cape Town where Palearctic waders winter in tens of thousands and Cape gannet pass offshore. The Postberg section opens for the spring wildflower season.
Wikipedia Cape Town Guide Map
Doñana National Park
Andalusia
UNESCO World Heritage SiteSpanish Imperial Eagle
Marsh, dune and cork oak woodland at the mouth of the Guadalquivir, holding a large part of Europe's wintering waterfowl and one of the last Spanish imperial eagle populations. Access to the core is by permit and guided vehicle only.
Wikipedia Seville Guide Map
Ebro Delta
Catalonia
Audouin's GullRice Paddies and Lagoons
A river delta of rice fields, lagoons and sand spits on the Catalan coast holding greater flamingo, Audouin's gull and a large slender-billed gull colony. Punta de la Banya is the core breeding area.
Wikipedia Map
Monfragüe National Park
Extremadura
Cinereous Vulture ColonyRoadside Raptor Watching
A quartzite gorge on the Tagus holding one of the world's largest cinereous vulture colonies, along with Spanish imperial eagle, Egyptian vulture and black stork. The Salto del Gitano viewpoint puts the cliff nests at eye level from the road.
Wikipedia Map
Sinharaja Forest Reserve
Sabaragamuwa
UNESCO World Heritage SiteMixed-Species Feeding Flocks
The island's last large tract of primary lowland rainforest, holding most of Sri Lanka's 34 endemic birds. Its mixed-species feeding flocks, led by the orange-billed babbler, are among the best studied anywhere.
Wikipedia Map
Falsterbo
Skåne
Autumn Raptor Bottleneck
A peninsula at Sweden's south-western tip where migrants funnel before the crossing to Denmark, producing dense autumn raptor passage from August to October. The bird observatory has ringed here since 1955.
Wikipedia Copenhagen Guide Map
Ngorongoro Conservation Area
Arusha Region
UNESCO World Heritage SiteCrater Soda Lake
A collapsed volcanic caldera whose floor holds a soda lake with lesser flamingo, plus grassland species such as kori bustard and rosy-throated longclaw. The crater rim forest adds a different set within a few kilometres.
Wikipedia Map
Kaeng Krachan National Park
Phetchaburi
Thailand's Largest National ParkOver 400 Species
Forest on the Tenasserim range against the Myanmar border, holding ratchet-tailed treepie, grey peacock-pheasant and all of Thailand's hornbill species. The Ban Krang and Panoen Thung camps are the standard bases.
Wikipedia Map
Asa Wright Nature Centre
Arima Valley, Trinidad
Veranda BirdingOilbird Colony
A former cocoa estate in the Northern Range whose veranda feeders draw tufted coquette, white-bearded manakin and a dozen hummingbird species before breakfast. A cave on the property holds one of the few accessible oilbird colonies.
Wikipedia Map
Caroni Swamp
Trinidad
Scarlet Ibis Roost
A mangrove lagoon where thousands of scarlet ibis come in to roost at dusk, turning the mangrove islands red. Boats leave in the late afternoon and time the return for the arrival.
Wikipedia Map
Bwindi Impenetrable Forest
Kanungu
UNESCO World Heritage SiteAlbertine Rift Endemics
Montane forest on the Albertine Rift holding around two dozen regional endemics, among them the African green broadbill and Grauer's warbler. The Mubwindi Swamp trail from Ruhija is the standard birding route.
Wikipedia Map
Mabamba Bay
Wakiso
ShoebillRamsar Wetland
A papyrus swamp on the northern shore of Lake Victoria an hour from Entebbe, and the most reliable place in Africa to see a shoebill. Local fishermen pole canoes through the channels at first light.
Wikipedia Map
Bempton Cliffs
Yorkshire, England
Half a Million SeabirdsEngland's Only Mainland Gannetry
Chalk cliffs on the Yorkshire coast holding around half a million seabirds between March and October, including England's only mainland northern gannet colony. Puffins, kittiwakes and guillemots nest within metres of the clifftop viewpoints.
Wikipedia Map
Isles of Scilly
Cornwall, England
October VagrantsAtlantic Landfall
An archipelago 45 kilometres off Land's End that acts as the first land for birds displaced across the Atlantic, producing a long list of North American vagrants each October. The islands are small enough to search on foot in a day.
Wikipedia Map
Bosque del Apache
New Mexico
Winter Crane and Snow Goose Roost
A managed Rio Grande wetland where tens of thousands of snow geese and sandhill cranes winter, leaving the roost ponds at sunrise in a single mass. The refuge loop road is drivable and open from November.
Wikipedia Map
Cape May
New Jersey
Autumn Hawk WatchSince 1976
A peninsula at the mouth of Delaware Bay where southbound raptors and songbirds pile up before the water crossing. The Cape May Hawkwatch platform has counted continuously each autumn since 1976.
Wikipedia Map
High Island
Texas
Trans-Gulf Migrant FalloutApril Peak
A salt dome carrying the only stand of tall woodland for miles on the upper Texas coast, so migrants arriving across the Gulf of Mexico drop into it. A north wind in April produces the fallouts the site is famous for.
Wikipedia Map
Madera Canyon
Arizona
Elegant Trogon15 Hummingbird Species
A sky-island canyon in the Santa Rita Mountains south of Tucson where Mexican species reach their northern limit, including elegant trogon and painted redstart. Lodge feeders here regularly draw more than a dozen hummingbird species in summer.
Wikipedia Map
Magee Marsh
Ohio
Boardwalk WarblersLake Erie Shore
A strip of beach ridge woodland on Lake Erie where warblers wait out the crossing to Canada, viewable at close range from a boardwalk through the trees. The first two weeks of May are the peak.
